items.prompt: How many 2-digit numbers can be divided exactly by 7?

options.why: Count from 14 to 98: that is 7 × 2 up to 7 × 14.
7 itself has only 1 digit, so start at 14.
The last one is 98 = 7 × 14. 105 has 3 digits.
Count again: 7 × 2 up to 7 × 14.

hints: Find the smallest and the largest 2-digit multiples of 7.
The smallest is 14 = 7 × 2. The largest is 98 = 7 × 14.
Count the whole numbers from 2 to 14.
items.explanation: The 2-digit multiples of 7 run from 7 × 2 = 14 to 7 × 14 = 98. That is 14 - 2 + 1 = 13 numbers.

items.prompt: A class of 6 must choose 2 pupils to be class monitors. How many different pairs can be chosen?

options.why: Each pupil can pair with 5 others, so there are more than 6 pairs.
Count again: 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1.
30 counts each pair twice: A with B and B with A.
A pupil cannot be paired with themselves.

hints: Name the pupils A to F.
A can pair with 5 others. B can pair with 4 new ones.
Add the new pairs for each pupil.
items.explanation: The new pairs are 5 for A, 4 for B, 3 for C, 2 for D and 1 for E. That is 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 15 pairs.

items.prompt: How many different triangles have whole-number side lengths and a perimeter of 12 cm?

options.why: 4, 4, 4 is a triangle, so there is at least 1.
4, 4, 4 works, but there are others.
Check 3, 4, 5 and 2, 5, 5 as well as 4, 4, 4.
Check each list: the two shorter sides must add up to more than the longest.

hints: In a triangle, the two shorter sides must add up to more than the longest side.
The longest side must be less than half of 12, so at most 5.
List the triples with longest side 5, then 4.
items.explanation: The longest side must be less than half of 12, so it is at most 5. The triangles are 2, 5, 5 and 3, 4, 5 and 4, 4, 4, which makes 3.

solution.say: Longest side less than half of 12.

items.prompt: A 4-digit number uses each of the digits 1, 2, 3 and 4 once. How many such numbers can be divided exactly by 4?

options.why: There are 3 good endings, not 1.
Each ending can have the front two digits in 2 orders.
Check the endings: 12, 24 and 32 all divide by 4.

hints: A number divides by 4 when its last two digits do.
Find the 2-digit endings from these digits that divide by 4.
The endings are 12, 24 and 32. The other two digits can go in 2 orders.
items.explanation: The last two digits must divide by 4: 12, 24 or 32. For each ending, the other two digits can go in 2 orders, so there are 3 × 2 = 6 numbers.

items.prompt: Eight friends split into two teams of 4 for a game. The teams have no names. How many different ways are there to split them?
hints: Look at the team that includes one particular friend, say Ana.
Ana's team needs 3 more players from the other 7 friends.
Count the ways to choose 3 from 7.
items.explanation: Ana's team needs 3 of the other 7 friends, and the rest form the other team. Choosing 3 from 7 can be done in 7 × 6 × 5 ÷ 6 = 35 ways.

solution.say: The order of the 3 does not matter.

items.prompt: A safe has a 3-digit code using the digits 0 to 9. Siti remembers the code is odd and all its digits are different. How many codes are possible?

options.why: The first digit of a code can be 0, so it has 9 choices once the last digit is picked.
The middle digit must differ from both other digits, so it has 8 choices.
500 counts every odd code, even with repeated digits.

hints: Fill in the last digit first.
The last digit must be odd: 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9.
Then the first digit can be any of the 9 digits left, and the middle any of the 8 left.
items.explanation: The last digit has 5 choices. The first digit can be any of the other 9 digits, and the middle one any of the remaining 8. That is 5 × 9 × 8 = 360 codes.

items.prompt: How many squares of all sizes are there on an 8 by 8 chessboard?
hints: Count each size of square separately.
There are 64 squares of size 1 and 49 of size 2.
A k by k square fits in (9 - k) × (9 - k) places.
items.explanation: The counts for sizes 1 to 8 are 64, 49, 36, 25, 16, 9, 4 and 1. Their sum is 204.

items.prompt: How many whole numbers from 1 to 1000 cannot be divided exactly by 2, by 3 or by 5?
hints: Count the numbers that can be divided by 2, 3 or 5, then subtract from 1000.
Use multiples of 2, 3 and 5, then of 6, 10 and 15, then of 30.
There are 500, 333 and 200 multiples of 2, 3 and 5.

solution.say: Remove numbers counted twice: multiples of 6, 10 and 15.
Add back multiples of 30, removed once too often.

items.prompt: Mira climbs 6 stairs. Each move she goes up 1, 2 or 3 stairs. In how many different ways can she reach the top?
hints: Work up from small staircases.
The ways for 1, 2 and 3 stairs are 1, 2 and 4.
The ways to reach a stair add the ways for the three stairs below it.
items.explanation: The ways for 1 to 6 stairs are 1, 2, 4, 7, 13 and 24, because each number is the sum of the three before it. So there are 24 ways.

items.prompt: Dewi has 6 shirts, 3 skirts and 2 hats. An outfit is one shirt, one skirt and one hat. How many different outfits can she make?
hints: For each shirt, count the skirts.
6 shirts and 3 skirts make 18 pairs.
Each pair can have 2 different hats.

options.why: You added 6 + 3 + 2. Outfits are made by choosing one of each, so multiply.
You multiplied only two of the numbers. A hat is chosen too.
Check the multiplying: 6 × 3 × 2.
This is 6 × 3 × 2 × 2. The hat count is only counted once.

items.prompt: A pizza shop has 5 toppings: cheese, onion, tomato, corn and mushroom. A customer picks exactly 2 different toppings. How many different pairs of toppings can be picked?
hints: List the pairs that start with cheese.
Cheese goes with 4 other toppings.
Onion has 3 new partners, because onion and cheese is already counted.
items.explanation: The pairs are 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10. Each pair is counted once because the order does not matter.

items.prompt: How many even 3-digit numbers can be made using only the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, if no digit is used twice in a number?
hints: Choose the last digit first. It must be even.
The last digit can be 2 or 4.
Then choose the first digit from the 4 left, and the middle from the 3 left.
items.explanation: The last digit has 2 choices, the first digit has 4 choices left, and the middle digit has 3. So 2 × 4 × 3 = 24 numbers.

options.why: You may have counted only the numbers ending in 2, or have left a place out.
Check the count of digits for each place. The last digit has 2 choices, then 4, then 3.
The first digit has 4 choices after the last digit is chosen, not 5.
This counts all 3-digit numbers with no repeated digit, not only the even ones.

items.prompt: A grid has 3 rows and 4 columns of small squares. How many rectangles of all sizes (squares count as rectangles) can be found in the grid?
hints: A rectangle is decided by choosing its left and right sides and its top and bottom sides.
There are 5 vertical lines and 4 horizontal lines.
Choose 2 of the 5 vertical lines, and 2 of the 4 horizontal lines.
items.explanation: Choosing 2 of 5 vertical lines gives 10 ways. Choosing 2 of 4 horizontal lines gives 6 ways. So there are 10 × 6 = 60 rectangles.

solution.say: Choosing 2 of 5 vertical lines gives 10 ways.
Choosing 2 of 4 horizontal lines gives 6 ways.

items.prompt: How many 3-digit numbers have digits that add up to 7?
hints: The first digit is at least 1.
List by the first digit: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 or 7.
If the first digit is 1, the other two digits add up to 6.
items.explanation: First digit 1: the other two add to 6, which gives 7 numbers. First digit 2: add to 5, giving 6 numbers. First digit 3: 5 numbers. First digit 4: 4 numbers. First digit 5: 3 numbers. First digit 6: 2 numbers. First digit 7: 1 number. 7 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 28.

items.prompt: Five friends sit in a row of five chairs. Ali and Bima must sit next to each other. In how many different ways can the five friends sit?
hints: Treat Ali and Bima as one block.
Now there are 4 things to arrange: the block and 3 friends.
Do not forget that Ali and Bima can swap places inside the block.
items.explanation: With the pair as one block, 4 things can be arranged in 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24 ways. Ali and Bima can swap, so 24 × 2 = 48 ways.

options.why: You treated Ali and Bima as one block but forgot they can swap places.
This is 5 × 4 × 3, not a count of full seating plans.

This is all the seating plans, with no limit on Ali and Bima.

mark: In how many different ways can the five friends sit?

solution.say: With the pair as one block, 4 things can be arranged in 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24 ways.
Ali and Bima can swap, so 24 × 2 = 48 ways.

items.prompt: Amara pays exactly Rp10.000 using only Rp1.000, Rp2.000 and Rp5.000 notes. She may use as many of each kind as she likes, and the order does not matter. In how many different ways can she pay?
hints: Count by the number of Rp5.000 notes: 0, 1 or 2.
With 2 notes of Rp5.000, there is only 1 way.
With 1 note of Rp5.000, pay Rp5.000 using Rp1.000 and Rp2.000 notes. With none, pay Rp10.000.
items.explanation: Two Rp5.000 notes: 1 way. One Rp5.000 note, then Rp5.000 left with Rp1.000 and Rp2.000: 0, 1 or 2 notes of Rp2.000 gives 3 ways. With no Rp5.000 note: 0 to 5 notes of Rp2.000 gives 6 ways. Total 1 + 3 + 6 = 10.

items.prompt: How many diagonals does a polygon with 7 sides have? (A diagonal joins two corners that are not next to each other.)
hints: From one corner, count the other corners it can join with a diagonal.
It cannot join itself or the 2 next to it.
Each diagonal is counted from both of its ends.
items.explanation: Each of the 7 corners joins to 4 corners by a diagonal, so 7 × 4 = 28. Each diagonal is counted twice, so 28 ÷ 2 = 14.

mark: How many diagonals does a polygon with 7 sides have?

solution.say: Each of the 7 corners joins to 4 corners by a diagonal, so 7 × 4 = 28.
Each diagonal is counted twice, so 28 ÷ 2 = 14.
